meta.description: Vitality Compass plan template configurations. Each template has 3 category variations (Beginner, Maintainer, Optimizer) with 4-week phased structures.

templates.title: Better Sleep
templates.description: Build a sleep routine that helps you fall asleep faster, stay asleep longer, and wake up feeling rested.

variations.description: Foundation — build the minimum viable sleep routine.
variations.weeklyCheckIn: How many nights this week did you hit your bedtime within 30 minutes?

actionItems: Pick a target bedtime and set a phone alarm for it.
Aim for 7 hours in bed minimum.
No other changes — just get into bed at the same time.
Add a 5-minute pre-bed wind-down routine.
Dim the lights, put your phone away, and do something calm (deep breathing, reading a physical book).
Keep it simple — the goal is consistency, not perfection.
Within 30 minutes of waking, get 5 minutes of natural light.
Open the curtains, step outside, or stand near a window.
Morning light signals your brain to set its internal clock for the day.
No caffeine after 2 PM.
Replace afternoon coffee/tea with herbal tea or water.
Notice how your sleep quality changes this week.

variations.description: Consistency + quality upgrades — take your sleep from okay to great.
variations.weeklyCheckIn: Rate your sleep quality this week (1–10) and note one thing that helped or hurt.

actionItems: Same bedtime and wake time every day (within 30 min), including weekends.
Your circadian rhythm relies on consistency — weekends included.
Set an alarm for both waking up AND going to bed.
No screens (phone, TV, laptop) for 30 minutes before bed.
Replace screen time with a book, journaling, or a podcast.
Use blue-light blocking mode if you absolutely must use a device.
Drop bedroom temperature to 65–68°F (18–20°C).
Add a fan, open a window, or switch to lighter bedding.
A cooler room signals your body it's time to sleep.
Move evening exercise to morning or early afternoon.
No vigorous activity within 2 hours of bedtime.
Gentle stretching or yoga in the evening is fine and may help.

variations.description: Bio-individual fine-tuning — optimize every variable for elite sleep.
variations.weeklyCheckIn: What's one adjustment you tried this week that improved your sleep? What didn't work?

actionItems: Use a sleep tracker or journal to log: bedtime, wake time, night wakings, and morning energy.
Identify patterns — what correlates with good vs bad sleep?
Focus on trends, not single-night data.
Wear blue-light blocking glasses 2 hours before bed.
Install blackout curtains or use a sleep mask.
Cover or remove all LED lights in the bedroom.
Last meal at least 3 hours before bedtime.
No large meals or alcohol within 2 hours of sleep.
If hungry before bed, have a small snack (e.g., banana, warm milk).
Create a full 30-minute wind-down routine.
Light stretching, gratitude journaling, progressive muscle relaxation.
Experiment to find the combination that works best for you.

templates.title: More Energy
templates.description: Boost your daily energy through nutrition, movement, and strategic habits — no caffeine crashes, no extreme diets.

variations.description: Foundations — energy through nutrition and hydration basics.
variations.weeklyCheckIn: On a scale of 1–10, how was your energy this week? What one change helped most?

actionItems: Drink 6 glasses of water per day.
Use a marked water bottle or set phone reminders.
Start each morning with a full glass of water.
Add protein to breakfast (egg, yogurt, nuts, protein shake).
Aim for at least 15–20g of protein at your first meal.
Protein stabilizes blood sugar and prevents mid-morning crashes.
Instead of reaching for caffeine/sugar at 3 PM, drink a glass of water.
Take a 5-minute walk or stretch break.
Notice if your energy naturally rebounds within 15 minutes.
Add one serving of vegetables or fruit to each meal.
Doesn't matter which kind — just add produce.
Frozen, fresh, or canned — they all count.

variations.description: Sustained energy through meal structure and movement snacks.
variations.weeklyCheckIn: Rate your energy dips throughout the day — when are they worst? Did this week's focus help?

actionItems: Structure eating into 3 meals + 1 snack.
No skipping meals — consistent fuel prevents energy crashes.
Set a loose schedule (e.g., 8 AM, 12 PM, 3 PM snack, 7 PM dinner).
Aim for 20–30g protein at each meal.
Include at least one palm-sized portion per main meal.
Good sources: chicken, fish, tofu, eggs, Greek yogurt, beans.
Take a 10-minute walk after lunch.
Post-meal movement blunts blood sugar spikes and prevents the afternoon slump.
Even a slow walk counts.
Identify one source of added sugar you consume daily.
Swap it for a lower-sugar alternative (e.g., soda → sparkling water).
Notice how your afternoon energy changes.

variations.description: Fine-tuning — timing, macros, and recovery for peak energy.
variations.weeklyCheckIn: What's your energy pattern this week? When do you feel most and least energized — and what's one hypothesis why?

actionItems: Log one full day of eating (no judgment, just data).
Note the protein/carb/fat balance at each meal.
Identify one gap or area for improvement.
Move most carbs to post-workout or evening meals.
Limit refined carbs earlier in the day.
Pair carbs with protein or fat to slow glucose absorption.
Optimize sleep timing for energy (reference Better Sleep plan).
Track how sleep quality predicts next-day energy levels.
Identify your personal "sleep sweet spot" (7, 7.5, 8, or 8.5 hours).
Limit caffeine to 1–2 cups, only before noon.
Observe whether afternoon energy improves without a second coffee.
Switch to herbal tea or decaf for the afternoon ritual.

templates.title: Stress Management
templates.description: Build resilience and calm through science-backed mindset practices — no toxic positivity, just practical tools.

variations.description: The 5-minute reset — micro-habits that shift your nervous system.
variations.weeklyCheckIn: How many days this week did you do your new habit? What got in the way?

actionItems: 3 times a day, take 1 slow deep breath (4s in, 4s out).
Attach it to an existing habit (before coffee, after bathroom, before bed).
That's it — one breath. No more, no pressure.
Once a day, sit in silence for 5 minutes.
No phone, no input, no agenda. Just be.
Set a timer so you don't have to watch the clock.
Each night, write down one thing that went well today.
One sentence minimum — no need to elaborate.
The gratitude can be tiny (e.g., 'good cup of coffee').
When you catch yourself worrying after 8 PM, say 'I'll deal with this tomorrow.'
Write it down in a notebook and close it.
This trains your brain to contain worry to appropriate times.

variations.description: Building a buffer — regular practices that build resilience.
variations.weeklyCheckIn: What's your stress level been this week (1–10)? Did your daily practice shift it at all?

actionItems: Before checking your phone in the morning, take 3 deep breaths.
Ask yourself: 'What do I need today?'
Notice the answer without judging it.
One 10-minute walk per day with no phone, no podcasts.
No purpose other than walking and being present.
Notice your surroundings — the air, the sounds, the ground beneath you.
Pick one daily activity and do only that — no multitasking.
Eat without scrolling. Commute without podcasts. Shower without planning.
Single-tasking for even 10 minutes gives your brain a recovery window.
10 minutes before bed: journal 3 things you accomplished today.
Write 1 thing you're releasing for tomorrow.
Close the notebook and let the day go.

variations.description: Advanced resilience — active recovery and mindset training.
variations.weeklyCheckIn: What's one stress pattern you noticed this week? Did your practice help you respond differently?

actionItems: 10-minute body scan meditation before bed (guided or self-led).
Notice tension in each part of your body without trying to fix it.
Awareness alone often helps the tension release naturally.
When you catch negative self-talk, write it down.
Ask: 'What would I tell a friend who said this to me?'
Write the kinder, more balanced version.
Identify one boundary you need to set (with work, a person, or yourself).
Practice saying 'no' or 'not right now' once this week.
Start small — a boundary with low stakes.
Review your week: where did you truly recover vs merely distract?
Truly recover = feel recharged, present, connected.
Merely distract = zone out, scroll, numbing.
Adjust one recovery window to be genuinely restorative this week.

templates.title: Balanced Wellness
templates.description: A gentle, full-body plan that touches all 4 wellness pillars equally. Perfect when you don't have a single priority area.

variations.weeklyCheckIn: How did this week feel? Which pillar was easiest to work on? Which was hardest?

actionItems: Drink 6 glasses of water daily.
Take 3 deep breaths (4s in, 4s out) at 3 points during the day.
No other changes — build the foundation first.
Walk for 5 minutes after lunch.
Add one serving of vegetables to one meal.
Small steps that compound.
Set a consistent bedtime and wake time.
Write down one good thing from your day before sleeping.
Sleep + gratitude = a powerful reset.
Continue your Week 1–3 habits.
Pick one area to focus on next month.
Reflect on what worked and what didn't.

variations.weeklyCheckIn: Which pillar feels strongest? Which needs more attention next week?

actionItems: Add protein to breakfast (20g+).
Eat vegetables with lunch AND dinner.
Drink water before every meal.
Walk for 10 minutes after lunch daily.
Do one strength session (bodyweight is fine).
Stand up and stretch every hour.
Stick to a consistent bedtime all 7 days.
No screens 30 min before bed.
Morning check-in: 3 breaths before phone.
Continue all pillars from weeks 1–3.
Identify which habit you want to keep permanently.
Set a goal for next month.

variations.weeklyCheckIn: What's your overall wellness score this week (1–10)? Which adjustment moved the needle most?

actionItems: Log one day of eating — identify one macro gap.
Eat your largest meal earlier in the day.
Finish eating 3 hours before bed.
Do 3 different types of movement this week.
One easy cardio, one strength, one mobility/flexibility.
Morning light + movement within 30 min of waking.
Sleep tracking audit — identify patterns.
Blue-blocking glasses 2h before bed.
Bedroom temperature at 65–68°F.
Daily structured journaling (3 gratitudes + 1 accomplishment + 1 intention).
Body scan meditation before bed.
Review the month — what habits will you keep?

categoryDescriptions.Beginner: New to wellness habits or has let them slide. Needs foundational, low-barrier steps. High support, low overwhelm.
categoryDescriptions.Maintainer: Has basic routines but inconsistent or stuck. Needs accountability, variety, and small upgrades to existing habits.
categoryDescriptions.Optimizer: Strong habits, good consistency. Needs advanced strategies, bio-individual tuning, and fresh challenges.
